newsitem.title: UK: CE ups Northern Electric stake to 19.9 pct.
newsitem.headline: CE ups Northern Electric stake to 19.9 pct.

text.p: CE Electric, the CalEnergy Co Inc unit bidding for Northern Electric Plc, bought 6.5 million shares in the UK utility, raising its stake in the firm to 19.9 percent, according to a statement released on Thursday.
CE bought the shares at its bid price of 630p per share, broker Hoare Govett said in a stock market disclosure statement.
Northern Electric's shares fell 5.5p to 625 in heavy trade by 1230 GMT, as rival "white knight" bidders failed to emerge to counter CE's hostile bid.
Northern Electric rejected CE's estimated 650 million stg bid last week, arguing that it undervalued the company.
Analysts expected the regional electricity supplier to report glowing half-year results soon in an attempt to support its case that CE's bid was too low.
CE Electric is 70 percent owned by Nebraska-based CalEnergy, with the rest held by U.S. construction to telecoms group Peter Kiewit Sons.
